remarks: Three systems are live, down from four — Gaenari made landfall at Quanzhou on 24 August and has dropped out of the JMA feed. Saudel is the only true typhoon left and is the one to watch: it has closed to 303 km from Shanghai/Ningbo inside 45 hours, against 414 km a run ago, and SEKO expects berthing freezes and pilotage halts along the Zhejiang and Shanghai coast into the weekend.

SEKO finally refreshed its monitor on 25 August after thirteen days, so the berth-wait figures on this page are current for the first time in a fortnight. They are worse than the stale ones they replace: Shanghai is now 8 to 9.5 days by terminal and Ningbo 5 to 6, with Meishan Island yard at 100 percent. SEKO also counts 139 containerships waiting at Shanghai, a near six-fold rise in two weeks, and roughly 500,000 TEU of omitted capacity across Asia-Europe, Transpacific and Asia-Latin America.

No tracked port changed operating status this run. Shanghai/Ningbo and Haiphong stay recovering, Xiamen and Shenzhen stay on watch. Xiamen's watch has been re-pointed from Gaenari, which is gone, to Saudel, which is not. Nothing was dropped and nothing new was added.

Two things worth flagging that sit outside this file's scope. Qingdao is running capital dredging at QQCTU berth 101 from 19 August for at least two weeks and is absorbing diversions from Shanghai and Ningbo, so a rising queue there is not weather. Busan is carrying roughly 2 days of berth delay purely from soaking up China omission cargo, with no system within 600 km.
